title: The assumptions underneath
summary: Working backwards from a conclusion to the ideas that hold it together.
question: Which assumption is doing the most work?

sections.heading: Make the starting point visible
paragraphs: This example is a framework for reviewing a model, not a valuation or an investment recommendation. It begins with the inputs rather than a desired output.

List the assumptions in plain language. Separate an observed fact from an estimate, and an estimate from a convenient simplification. Someone reading the work should be able to find those distinctions without reverse-engineering a spreadsheet.
prompts: What is measured, and what is assumed?
Which estimate has the weakest evidence?
What changes if that estimate is wrong?

sections.heading: Explore a range of stories
paragraphs: Build a small number of internally consistent scenarios. Give each one a narrative that explains how its inputs belong together. A scenario is a way to ask a question; it is not a claim about what will happen.
Use sensitivity checks to identify the inputs that deserve more research. Avoid choosing a precise number simply because the model produces one.

sections.heading: Keep an audit trail
paragraphs: Record the date of the exercise, the sources of the inputs, and the reason for revisions. When new information arrives, that history makes it easier to distinguish a changed fact from a changed interpretation.
A clear model helps a reader inspect the reasoning. Its usefulness comes from transparency, not from the apparent certainty of its output.
